cards.title: The 5 Arabic Negation Pairings
cards.summary: In Arabic, each time-frame locks onto its own negation particle — and that particle controls the verb ending.

diagram.danger: ✗ لَا + Past (لَا ذَهَبْتُ) = Wish / Curse (e.g. لَا قَدَّرَ اللهُ "May Allah forbid"), NEVER factual "didn't"!

rows.col4: Standard MSA & Qur'ān (لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ)

cards.trap: Never pair لَا with a past verb for ordinary negation: ✗ لَا ذَهَبْتُ is ungrammatical for "I didn't go". Always use لَمْ أَذْهَبْ or مَا ذَهَبْتُ.

quickCheck.prompt: Say "I did not go to work" in BOTH valid Arabic ways — and remember why لَا ذَهَبْتُ is never used:
quickCheck.answerAr: لَمْ أَذْهَبْ إِلَى العَمَلِ  /  مَا ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى العَمَلِ
quickCheck.tr: lam adhhab ilā l-ʿamali  /  mā dhahabtu ilā l-ʿamali
quickCheck.answerEn: لَمْ + short present OR مَا + past verb (never ✗ لَا + past, which expresses a wish/curse).

cards.title: How Arabic Marks Past, Present & Future
cards.summary: Past tense glues "who" onto the BACK of the root; Present glues "who" onto the FRONT; Future simply clips سَـ onto Present.
cards.trap: Don't mix front and back markers at the same time (never ✗ أَذْهَبْتُ). Pick BACK for past (ذَهَبْتُ) or FRONT for present (أَذْهَبُ).

quickCheck.prompt: Flip "I read the Qur'an" across Past → Present → Future:
quickCheck.answerAr: قَرَأْتُ القُرْآنَ ← أَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ ← سَأَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ
quickCheck.answerEn: Past = suffix ـتُ (قَرَأْتُ); Present = prefix أَ (أَقْرَأُ); Future = سَـ + present (سَأَقْرَأُ).

cards.title: The 3 Arabic Words for "Price / Cost"
cards.summary: English says "price/cost" for almost everything; Arabic cleanly separates intrinsic value, shop rate, and service fare.

lanes.title: Intrinsic Value / Worth
lanes.desc: What an item is truly worth or paid for in exchange (Qur'ān & classic prose).

lanes.title: Market Sticker / Rate
lanes.desc: The listed shop price, menu rate, or market quote.

lanes.title: Service Fare / Rent / Wage
lanes.desc: Payment for transport, labour, or hiring space (never a physical object).

rows.col4: Handing money for goods; Qur'ān 2:41 (ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا)
Asking how much something costs in a shop or market
Taxi rides, bus tickets, delivery fees (root أ-ج-ر ajr reward!)

cards.trap: Never ask a taxi driver for السِّعْر — ask كَمِ الأُجْرَةُ؟ ("How much is the fare?"). Notice أُجْرَة shares root أ-ج-ر with أَجْر (divine reward/wage).

quickCheck.prompt: Which word do you ask a shopkeeper vs a taxi driver?
quickCheck.answerAr: فِي السُّوقِ: كَمِ السِّعْرُ؟  /  فِي السَّيَّارَةِ: كَمِ الأُجْرَةُ؟
quickCheck.tr: kami s-siʿru (shop) vs kami l-ujratu (taxi fare)
quickCheck.answerEn: سِعْر = shop/market tag; أُجْرَة = taxi fare/service fee; ثَمَن = value/sum paid.

cards.title: Pronoun Endings: Mine, For Me, & Him vs Her (-ka / -ki)
cards.summary: Arabic rarely leaves "my / me / your" as separate words — one tiny ending on a noun, preposition, or verb does the whole job.

lanes.title: 1st Person Attachment
lanes.desc: Noun + ـِي = my (كِتَابِي) · Prep + ـِي = for/with me (لِي / عِنْدِي) · Verb + ـنِي = me (سَاعَدَنِي)

lanes.title: Speaking to a Man
lanes.desc: Short fatḥah (-a): كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ · مَا اسْمُكَ؟ · هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ؟

lanes.title: Speaking to a Woman (e.g. Saba)
lanes.desc: Short kasrah (-i): كَيْفَ كَانَ يَوْمُكِ؟ · هَلْ يُمْكِنُكِ؟ (Same spelling, vowel flips!)

rows.col4: Drop الـ when adding a possessive suffix
لِـ + ـِي = لِي (for me/mine); عِنْدَ + ـِي = عِنْدِي (I have)
ـكَ (-ka) to a man · ـكِ (-ki) to Saba / a woman

cards.trap: Never keep الـ on a word that has a possessive ending: say كِتَابِي (my book), never ✗ الكِتَابِي!

quickCheck.prompt: How do you ask Saba "How was your day?" vs asking a male colleague?
quickCheck.answerAr: لِزَوْجَتِكَ: كَيْفَ كَانَ يَوْمُكِ؟  /  لِلرَّجُلِ: كَيْفَ كَانَ يَوْمُكَ؟
quickCheck.tr: kayfa kāna yawmuki (-ki fem.) vs yawmuka (-ka masc.)
quickCheck.answerEn: ـكِ (-ki with kasrah) for her; ـكَ (-ka with fatḥah) for him.

cards.title: Possession (Idāfah) vs Noun + Adjective
cards.summary: Where الـ sits tells you everything: "the" on the SECOND word only = "X of the Y"; "the" on BOTH words = "the [adjective] X".

lanes.title: Possession Bridge (إِضَافَة)
lanes.desc: مِفْتَاحُ الغُرْفَةِ = "the key OF the room" (Word 1 is bare; Word 2 takes ـِ kasrah).

lanes.title: Noun + Adjective (نَعْت)
lanes.desc: الغُرْفَةُ الجَدِيدَةُ = "the new room" (Adjective comes AFTER noun & mirrors الـ, gender, case).

cards.trap: Never say ✗ المِفْتَاحُ الغُرْفَةِ for "the room key" — the first word of an idāfah bridge NEVER wears الـ!

quickCheck.prompt: Say "the room key" in Arabic — where does الـ go?
quickCheck.answerEn: الـ goes ONLY on the second word (الغُرْفَةِ); مِفْتَاحُ stays bare.

cards.title: High-Value Minimal Pairs: One Dot Changes Everything
cards.summary: Locking look-alike pairs side-by-side stops silent mix-ups in both everyday speech and Qur'ānic listening.

lanes.title: أَعُودُ (Return) vs أَعُوذُ (Seek Refuge)
lanes.desc: Plain د (ع-و-د) = I return home · Dotted ذ (ع-و-ذ) = I seek refuge in Allah (Al-Falaq / An-Nās).

lanes.title: جَوْزَة (Walnut) vs زَوْجَة (Wife)
lanes.desc: ج leads the crunchy walnut snack (جَوْزَة) · ز leads your spouse/partner (زَوْجَة)!

lanes.title: حَفْلَة (Party) vs أُرَتِّبُ (I Tidy)
lanes.desc: حَفْلَة shares root with Bengali মাহফিল (mahfil gathering) · أُرَتِّبُ shares root with tartīb (neat order).

rows.col4: Plain د = return to your door; dotted ذ = أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ

quickCheck.prompt: Contrast أَعُودُ vs أَعُوذُ — and what is the Jumu'ah prayer greeting "May Allah accept"?
quickCheck.answerAr: أَعُودُ (أَرْجِعُ إِلَى البَيْتِ) vs أَعُوذُ (بِاللهِ)  ·  تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ
quickCheck.tr: aʿūdu (return) vs aʿūdhu (seek refuge) · taqabbala llāh
quickCheck.answerEn: Plain د = return home; dotted ذ = seek refuge; تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ = May Allah accept (kobul).

cards.title: Surah An-Nās Anatomy: Why الصُّدُور (Chests) and Not القُلُوب (Hearts)?
cards.summary: In Qur'ānic precision, the whisperer (الوَسْوَاس الخَنَّاس) can only pace the outer courtyard (الصَّدْر); he cannot enter the locked heart (القَلْب) unless invited.

diagram.outer: الصَّدْر (aṣ-ṣadr — Outer Courtyard / Chest): Where الوَسْوَاس الخَنَّاس throws passing whispers (يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ).
diagram.shield: 🛡️ ذِكْرُ اللهِ (Remembrance of Allah): The instant you remember Allah, الخَنَّاس shrinks back & retreats!
diagram.inner: ❤️ القَلْب / الفُؤَاد (al-qalb — Inner Sanctuary / Heart): Seat of īmān — locked to Shayṭān unless the gate is opened.

rows.col4: Onomatopoeic rustle: repetitive, subtle inner muttering
Cowardly slinker: retreats upon dhikr, creeps back in heedlessness
Ṣudūr = outer foyer/chests (accessible to passing thoughts), NOT qulūb!
Tied knots (same root as ʿaqd contract & ʿaqīdah creed)

quickCheck.prompt: In Surah An-Nās, why does Allah say فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ (in the chests) rather than قُلُوب (hearts), and what makes الخَنَّاس retreat?
quickCheck.answerAr: الصَّدْرُ هُوَ السَّاحَةُ الخَارِجِيَّةُ، وَيَخْنِسُ الشَّيْطَانُ عِنْدَ ذِكْرِ اللهِ
quickCheck.answerEn: الصَّدْر (chest) is the outer courtyard around القَلْب (the heart), and الخَنَّاس slinks back whenever Allah is remembered.

cards.title: The Polite Request & Conversation Control Ladder
cards.summary: Four reusable sentence frames let you ask for anything, request help politely, or slow a fast speaker down without switching to English.

rows.col4: Bridge word أَنْ flips verb ending from -u to -a
Pair with لَمْ أَفْهَمْ، كَرِّرْ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (I didn't understand, repeat please)

quickCheck.prompt: How do you politely ask "Can you help me?" and "Speak slowly, please" in Arabic?
quickCheck.answerAr: هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ مُسَاعَدَتِي؟  ·  تَكَلَّمْ بِبُطْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
quickCheck.tr: hal yumkinuka musāʿadatī? · takallam bi-buṭʾin min faḍlika
quickCheck.answerEn: يُمْكِنُكَ (mumkin) + مُسَاعَدَتِي (my aid); تَكَلَّمْ بِبُطْءٍ (speak with slowness).

cards.title: The 7-Day Number Root Map & Telling Time
cards.summary: Five days of the Arabic week literally count 1 to 5 from Sunday, Friday means "Gathering", and clock hours use feminine ordinal adjectives.

nodes.sub: Same root as اجْتِمَاع (meeting) & مَسْجِد جَامِع

rows.col4: Sunday is for the Arabic lesson

cards.trap: Exception on the clock: 1 o'clock uses الوَاحِدَة (السَّاعَةُ الوَاحِدَةُ), while 2:00–10:00 follow the clean الثَّانِيَة / الثَّالِثَة / السَّابِعَة / الثَّامِنَة pattern!

quickCheck.prompt: Why is Thursday called الخَمِيس and Friday called الجُمُعَة — and how do you say "at 7 o'clock"?
quickCheck.answerEn: Sunday–Thursday count 1–5 (أحد..خميس); الجُمُعَة = assembly (ج-م-ع); clock hours take feminine ordinals (السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ).
